body:
## Problem
While paused, `ShaderEngine.tick` still drew a full frame on every animation frame ("so parameter edits stay visible"). That had two effects:
- **Feedback buffers kept evolving** behind a "paused" label: simulations and trails didn't actually stop.
- **The main thread stayed busy** for nothing. On a machine without a GPU (CI runners, the e2e container) a paused page ran at about 4 frames a second, and an idle callback waited 8.5 s. That is what starved Monaco's highlighting in #42.

## Change
Paused now means a still frame. The engine draws only when something visible changed:
- **Frame requests:** each of these asks for two frames, one into each target of a feedback buffer, via a new `requestFrames()`:
  - a parameter
  - the shader
  - a channel or channel texture
  - a decoded texture
  - a resize
  - the effects chain or its scope, including the chain's asynchronous module load and debounced custom-effect compiles (new `PostProcessing.onChanged`)
  - a click on the canvas
  - the end of a capture
  - a restored context
- **Profiler:** it keeps drawing while enabled, because it measures frames.
- **Shader-switch reveal:** `ShaderCanvas` requests the frames its reveal waits on (`SETTLE_FRAMES`), so the transition still fades in while paused.
- **fps readout:** it counts frames actually drawn, so a still preview reads 0.
- **Unchanged:** a running preview, captures, and `screenshot()`, which already draws explicitly.

## Measured, in the e2e browser (software WebGL)
| Paused preview | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wait for an idle callback | 8.5 s | 11 ms |
| Animation frames per second | 4 | 61 |
| Full e2e suite | 6.0 min | 1.7 min |

## Tests
- New `paused-redraw.spec.ts` (9 tests, fake GL):
  - every frame draws while playing, and none once paused, though one frame stays scheduled
  - feedback buffers are frozen while paused
  - exactly two frames after each kind of change, a resize and a click
  - `requestFrames(n)` draws `n` frames
  - the profiler keeps frames coming
  - the fps readout reads 0 when still
  - resuming draws every frame again
- Rendering specs: 198 pass. Studio web suite: 847 pass. Lint, format and typecheck are clean.
- Full e2e suite: 5 of 5 pass, including `shader-switch`, which pauses and then switches shaders, so the reveal is covered.

body:
## Problem
The code editor sometimes showed GLSL as plain, uncoloured text until the first scroll. It reproduces on `develop` before the plugin-themes work too.

## Root cause
The tokenizer itself works: `monaco.editor.tokenize` and `colorizeModelLine` return keyword and type tokens. Monaco colours a model in two ways:
- **Visible lines**, at once, when the view tells it which they are: on a scroll, a view-state restore, or the editor's creation.
- **Everything else**, in the background, in `requestIdleCallback` with no timeout (`DefaultBackgroundTokenizer` in `textModelTokens.js`).

The preview renders on every frame. On a slow machine (measured in the CI container: about 4 frames a second, even paused) an idle callback never fires unless its timeout forces it; one queued with an 8 s timeout ran only after 8.5 s. The background pass therefore never runs, and its `backgroundTokenizationState` stays "in progress". A resize, or a newly mounted document without saved view state, changes what is on screen without telling Monaco, so those lines stay uncoloured until a scroll reports them.

## Fix
`CodeEditor` re-reports its viewport through the public `saveViewState`/`restoreViewState` pair, which moves nothing. This happens after the editor is created, after mounting a document that has no saved view state, and after every layout change, coalesced to one per animation frame. Edits were already handled once Monaco knows the visible lines.

## Tests
- New e2e `apps/studio-e2e/src/editor-highlighting.spec.ts`: opens the editor and asserts that the `uniform` keyword gets its own span, with a colour different from the editor's plain text. It **fails without the fix**, because each line is one uncoloured span, and passes with it.
- `pnpm lint`, the studio and e2e typechecks, and the studio web suite (838 tests) pass.

## Not in scope
The render loop still takes most of the main thread even while playback is paused, on a machine without a GPU. That probably deserves its own look.

body:
Implements the plan on `plans/plugin-themes`, tasks 01 and 02. A local `.sgplugin.json` can now ship colour themes for the app and the code editor. A chosen theme survives reloads and restarts. When its package is unavailable, the app falls back cleanly to the built-in theme.

## Shared contract (task 01)
- New `theme` contribution kind (`schemaVersion: 1`, `scheme: light | dark`). It carries a closed list of UI colour roles: 16 required and 18 optional. It also carries an editor palette whose `base` must match the scheme. Colours are opaque `#RRGGBB` only. Unknown fields, roles and tokens are refused, so no CSS, URL, font or script can come from a package. The existing quotas still apply.
- `protocolVersion` stays at 1, because themes add no Worker call. A package now needs `code` only for importers and exporters, and code is refused in a purely declarative package. Existing packages, ISF included, stay valid.
- Persistable reference `plugin:<packageId>/<contributionId>`, parsed strictly from the existing id patterns. New `appThemeId` sanitizer, defaulting to `builtin`. The editor theme preference accepts plugin references alongside `auto` and every existing built-in id.

## Studio (task 02)
- A root `AppThemes` service starts at startup on web and desktop. It is the single writer of the root `color-scheme`, the `--mat-sys-*` colour tokens and Monaco's global theme. `Preferences` no longer writes the scheme.
- A plugin theme brings its own scheme and leaves the remembered light/dark/system setting for the built-in. Before applying a theme, every token the previous one set is cleared. Optional roles a theme leaves out fall back to the built-in value for its scheme.
- The catalogue lists only themes from active, valid, compatible packages of the current profile. A stored reference outlives the asynchronous plugin load, but applies only while its theme is in the catalogue. Disabling, removing, replacing or an incompatible package, and a profile change, all restore the built-in. Installing or enabling a package selects nothing. No plugin Worker is started for themes.
- Monaco: plugin palettes are defined before they are selected, whether Monaco loads before or after the catalogue. A same-id update redefines the palette. Editor `auto` follows the app's palette, plugin themes included. Explicit editor choices and the settings dialog's preview, cancel and apply all keep working.
- UI: one shared, keyboard-navigable Theme submenu (`menuitemradio` items with swatches) replaces three duplicated menus: the web More menu, the desktop title bar and the preview menu. The command palette lists installed themes too. The editor settings list installed editor palettes. Plugins shows theme contributions with a swatch and a "Use as app theme" action. Labels are in English and French. No AAA badge is shown for plugin themes.
- Fixture: Grove Amber (`tools/workspace/fixtures/plugins/themes/grove-amber.sgplugin.json`), an original light and dark pair with no code.

## Tests
- Shared: `themes.spec.ts` and `editor-theme-reference.spec.ts` (31 tests with `package.spec.ts`).
- Studio: `themes/theme-catalog.spec.ts`, `themes/app-themes.spec.ts`, plus new cases in `preferences.spec.ts`. These cover lifecycle, profile switching, same-id updates, Monaco load order, preview and cancel, and a check that no Worker starts.
- E2E: `apps/studio-e2e/src/plugin-themes.spec.ts` asserts computed colours of the chrome, the menu overlay and Monaco across a real file import, enabling, keyboard selection, a reload, editor preview and cancel, an explicit editor palette, a same-id update, a partial palette, ISF alongside, removal and a signed-out profile.

## Verification run
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build:all`, `pnpm smoke:ssr`: pass. `pnpm format:check` is clean for every changed file.
- `pnpm build:desktop` and `pnpm pack:desktop`: pass. The packaged app, driven under xvfb, kept Grove Amber across an offline restart, and no plugin sandbox was created.
- New e2e spec: passes. The existing `shader-switch.spec.ts` also fails in the run container on the unchanged base `2fff989`, so that failure is environmental and not caused by this PR.

## Notes
- The fixture declares `appVersionRange: ">=1.4.0 <2.0.0"`, because `APP_VERSION` is still 1.4.0 and is managed by release-please. A 1.4.0 host refuses the `theme` kind explicitly.
- Deferred, as in the plan: a public catalogue, third-party theme packs, theme authoring and VS Code import, removing the flash before first paint, and syncing native windows.
- Pre-existing and not addressed here: GLSL syntax highlighting does not render in the editor, with built-in themes too, on the base commit.

body:
## Summary

New Nx project `apps/studio-e2e` (`@shadergrove/studio-e2e`) running Playwright against the studio dev server.

- **Server isolation**: `ng serve` on port 4322 (the smoke uses 4321), `reuseExistingServer: false`, no HMR or live reload. `src/serve.ts` starts it on a throwaway SQLite store, wipes the store on start and again once the server stops. `DATABASE_URL` is set to an empty string so PostgreSQL can't take over, and `BETTER_AUTH_URL` / `AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` are both set to the test origin. Verification, the HIBP check and the rate limit are turned off.
- **Auth**: a `setup` project (`auth.setup.ts`) signs up once through the API and saves `storageState` to `.auth/` (gitignored). The `chromium` project depends on it.
- **Fixture**: a signed-in `page` that fails the test on any `pageerror`.
- **Spec** `shader-switch.spec.ts` covers the freeze fixed in `RoutingCoordinator.onStandalonePage`. It opens Aurora Veil, clicks Hex Pulse and then Warp Tunnel, and goes Back, Back, Forward. After each step it checks three things: the exact `/shaders/<id>` (the id comes from `/api/shaders`), the single `aria-current` row, and the `.doc-name` title. To show the page still responds, it then filters the library and checks the row count. The test uses explicit timeouts and doesn't use fixed sleeps or `networkidle`.
- **Nx**: the `e2e` target is uncached and depends on `@shadergrove/studio:gen:ipc`, so `pnpm e2e` works from a fresh install. `implicitDependencies` on the studio marks the project as affected when the app changes. There is also a `typecheck` target.
- **Repo**: adds a root `pnpm e2e` script, and `test-results/`, `playwright-report/` and `.auth/` to `.gitignore`, oxlint and oxfmt.
- **CI**: new `E2E` job on Ubuntu. It uploads `playwright-report/` and `test-results/` when it fails. HTML reporter, `retries: 0`, one worker. The UI smoke job is unchanged.

The lockfile also has a small sass peer-variant dedup that pnpm made by itself during install.

## Verification

- `pnpm e2e` with the fix: 2 passed.
- Negative control in a temporary worktree, with only the `untracked()` wrapper removed from `onStandalonePage`: the test **fails** at the first library click (`expected /shaders/hex-pulse, received /shaders/aurora-veil`). Setup and the initial open both pass.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, and `tsc` for the new project all pass.

On Windows, Playwright force-kills the server, so the store directory stays until the next run wipes it. On Linux, the `SIGTERM` graceful shutdown removes it.

Web/SSR, the NestJS API and Electron now live in one application package, `apps/studio` (`@shadergrove/studio`). The API and IPC contract packages only served this application, so their code is now local to studio. `libs/backend` and `libs/shared` remain separate for their actual consumers in maintenance and MCP; their contents are unchanged.

The resulting application layout is:
- `src/app`: Angular UI and renderer adapters.
- `src/server/api`: NestJS modules, authentication, HTTP policies and API tests.
- `src/desktop/main` and `src/desktop/preload`: Electron lifecycle and bridge exposure.
- `src/desktop/contracts`: plain IPC types and the generated bridge.

Workspace commands, dependency declarations, lockfile importers, TypeScript/test discovery, Rollup, IPC checks, Nx, Docker, CI, editor configuration and documentation follow the new layout. API and Electron tests remain separate Node suites; Angular excludes their source tests. Import restrictions reject server/Electron imports in the renderer and permit only type imports of the generated bridge. Root Angular targets generate IPC first, and cached builds/checks hash its output. Both Rollup and the standalone generator write to `./src/desktop/contracts/ipc-bridge.ts`.

Existing root commands, build output directories and desktop installation identities are preserved. Resolved dependency package and snapshot records are unchanged.

Validation:
- Frozen-lockfile installation, lint and formatting passed.
- i18n, fonts and IPC stability checks passed; the bridge contains 9 modules, 65 channels and 8 emitted events.
- All workspace typechecks passed, including the Node API and Electron configurations.
- 85 API tests and 115 Electron tests passed after their relocation.
- 5 focused Angular desktop integration/sign-in tests passed with Node 26.5.0.
- Temporary lint probes confirmed that bridge type imports are allowed and runtime bridge, server and Electron imports are rejected; the probes were removed.
- The web production build and `pnpm smoke:ssr` passed. Removing the ignored generated bridge and running `pnpm build` also passed: Nx regenerated it before compilation.
- `pnpm smoke` passed, including offline fonts and plugin sandbox checks.
- `pnpm pack:win` passed and produced the unpacked Windows application with the relocated IPC bridge.

Also fixes the test-job hang introduced by PR #38 (commit `23cfd89`): reading `Router.currentNavigation()` inside the selection effect subscribed it to its own navigations and caused a routing feedback loop. Read the pending navigation with `untracked()` so standalone pages remain protected without adding a reactive dependency. The unchanged routing tests hung in isolation before the fix; all 3 now pass and exit. The complete Angular suite now passes: 810 tests in 70 files. The root `pnpm test` command also passes all five project targets and exits successfully in 42.4 seconds, with Nx caching disabled. Docker is not available locally; the existing PR Docker and Windows jobs remain in place.

body:
Tasks 02 and 03 of `docs/feature-plans/local-isf-plugins` (after #35 package/host, #36 custom effects, #37 MCP v3).

## Plugins / Installed (task 02)

- `/plugins` page (lazy route, toolbar link): review a `.sgplugin.json` before install (manifest, contributions, compatibility with `APP_VERSION`), install **disabled**, enable/disable, remove.
- Durable storage per profile:
  - web: IndexedDB `shadergrove-plugins:<userId|anonymous>`; the profile is only resolved once the auth session is known, so a reload never shows the anonymous partition first;
  - desktop: `<userData>/plugins/<sha256(id)[0:32]>.json`, atomic writes, IPC refused unless the sender is the main window.
- Records are re-validated on every load; a corrupted or now-incompatible record is listed as a problem and can still be removed.
- Contributions in use:
  - **effect** (declarative): copied into the current shader's post-processing chain after an off-screen probe compile (`ShaderEngine.probeCustomEffect`); the copy does not depend on the plugin (removing the plugin keeps it);
  - **importer**: file picked on the page → runs in the sandboxed host → `validateEffectCandidate` → same adoption path;
  - **exporter**: choose a custom effect of the current shader → file saved via `saveExport` (desktop, new `files:save-export` IPC with extension/size checks) or a download (web).
- `APP_VERSION` lives in `libs/shared/src/version.ts`, bumped by release-please (`extra-files`).

## ISF package (task 03)

- `tools/workspace/fixtures/plugins/isf/`: manifest + Worker code + `isf.sgplugin.json` generated by `pnpm generate:isf-plugin`; a web spec fails if the generated file drifts from its sources.
- Import of one-pass ISF FX filters (`inputImage` + float/bool/long/color inputs) into a custom effect, using the preprocessor only (`isf_main`, `IMG_*`, `TIME`, `RENDERSIZE`, per-input macros). Multi-pass, sized or persistent passes, extra image inputs, point2D/audio/event inputs and generators are refused with a clear message.
- Export back to `.fs` (round trip preserved through header/source markers; native custom effects get a generated ISF wrapper).

## Bundle

Plugin code imports `@shadergrove/shared/plugin` and `@shadergrove/shared/version` (new subpath exports) instead of the root barrel: importing the barrel from a lazy chunk made esbuild hoist it — with zod and the MCP protocol — into the initial bundle (2.25 MB, over the 2.2 MB budget). Initial total is back to 1.88 MB, same as `develop`. The routing coordinator treats the in-flight navigation as standalone, so a cold deep link to the lazy `/plugins` route is not normalized back to the editor.

## Validation

## Summary
Follow-up to #36. That PR changed the render schema that both the app and the MCP server validate:
- every effect has a required `instanceId`;
- the effect union gained a `custom` member.

`MCP_BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stayed at 2, so mismatched versions failed command by command, with an opaque `INTERNAL: The app's response to "…" did not match its schema`:

- **New server with a 1.4.0 app:** fails on every render, since every shader has a Bloom and 1.4.0 sends no ids.

## Summary
Phase 1 of `plans/custom-postprocess-effects` (tasks 01–03). Prerequisite for the local ISF plugin milestone, waves 02/03.

- **Contract (shared):** every effect gets an `instanceId`, and every chain helper targets it, so two instances of one type are set, moved, toggled and removed separately. Legacy effects take their type as id, the same on every load. A new `custom` effect embeds `{ apiVersion, name, source, controls }` plus its own values. A newer `apiVersion` is kept but not run. Code over the limit or invalid v1 controls are refused on save/import (`validateRenderStrict`) instead of being dropped. Bundles move to `shader-studio/v4`; v1–v3 still import. No SQL migration: `renderJson` already stores the whole render.
- **Renderer:** passes are keyed by `instanceId` and the composer's pass list is re-synced in place:
  - values are uniform pushes;
  - reorder, enable and add reuse built passes;
  - new custom code compiles one candidate on a 1×1 probe (shared with `PassCompiler`).
  
  A rejected edit keeps the last valid program. Code that never compiled is left out, with a diagnostic on `@effect/<id>`. Two context losses within 30 s suspend custom effects until Ctrl+Enter.
- **UI:**
  - The rack is keyed by instance: add any type more than once, duplicate, move (buttons or drag), reset, remove.
  - Custom effects show their local controls and compile errors with the author's line.
  - A Monaco dialog edits name, GLSL (debounced into the draft) and controls JSON, with revert.

body:
## What this adds

Public Explore, phase 1, web only and **off by default** (`PUBLIC_EXPLORE_ENABLED=1` turns it on).

- A verified owner publishes a frozen snapshot of a saved shader from My Shaders. Private edits never change it; only an explicit update does.
- Anyone can browse `/explore`, open `/explore/:id` at a stable URL, and run a preview on request. No session, no sign-in prompt.
- A verified account can copy a public shader into its own library (always a new private shader, with the source credited) or report it.
- Moderators, named by account id in `PUBLIC_EXPLORE_ADMIN_USER_IDS`, can hide or restore publications, resolve reports, restrict or restore a publisher, and read the history at `/admin/publications`.

The API contract is in `docs/public-explore-api.md`.

## How it is put together

- **Storage** (`libs/backend/src/publication`): six additive tables, migration 4 on both engines, queried through one portable SQL store. A snapshot is cut inside a transaction that holds the shader row, so sources, presets and image bytes belong to the same moment. Deleting the source shader or the account cascades to everything public; the audit trail is kept.
- **Visibility** is `ownerVisible && !moderatorHidden`, written by disjoint statements, so an owner cannot publish their way out of a takedown and a restore cannot undo an unpublish.
- **API** (`apps/server/src/publication`): with the flag off the routes are not registered at all; only `/api/capabilities` answers. Publication reads are `no-store`. Cookie-authenticated writes are checked against the trusted origins, which Better Auth only does for its own endpoints.
- **Web** (`apps/web/src/app/publications`, `apps/web/src/app/admin`): the pages are laid over the running editor rather than replacing it, so an unsaved draft survives a trip to Explore. Entry points appear only when the server says so; nothing is fetched during SSR, on the desktop or in the output window.

## Verification

- Lint, typecheck, all test suites, `build:all`, `smoke:ssr` and `build:desktop` pass locally.
- 45 browser checks against the built server cover the plan's six journeys: publish/discover/copy, private edits and racing writes, hide/restore, reports and authorization, publisher restriction, unsaved work and session changes. Flag-off, the output window and account switching were checked separately.
- The packaged desktop app, offline, shows no Explore entry points and makes no Explore requests.

## Not verified

- **PostgreSQL.** No database was available, so the Postgres suites were skipped, not passed. `postgres-repository.spec.ts` now also runs the publication suite and drops the whole schema between tests; that cleanup change is untested too. Please run with `SHADER_TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointing at a disposable database before merging.

## Worth knowing while reviewing

- Deleting a private shader deletes its publication, and so does an overwrite import of the same id. A re-created shader gets a new public id with no moderation history.
- Once a desktop library has been opened by a build with migration 4, older desktop builds refuse to open it. Turning the flag off does not undo that.
- Rate limits (publish, copy, report) are per process, like the existing sign-in limiter.
- `reportWorkspaceError` no longer raises a toast for a 401: the sign-in dialog is the message in the editor, and on Explore an anonymous visitor is owed neither.

Task 02 of the studio visual refresh, milestone 1. Restyles the app through Material's public theme inputs only: neutral chrome, cyan accent, small corners, compact desktop density and more opaque overlays.

**Stacked on #29.** This branch contains #29's two commits; after #29 merges, only `c5bea40` remains in the diff.

## Changes (`styles.scss`)
- **Surfaces:** `mat.theme-overrides` sets neutral graphite surfaces, text and outlines in dark mode and pale neutral ones in light mode, all through `light-dark()`, which removes the blue tint the cyan palette gave the neutrals. Selection (`secondary-container`) is a quiet tint of the accent.
- **Shape:** 4px controls and 8px dialogs; buttons and icon buttons lose the pill shape.
- **Density:** -2 only under `(pointer: fine) and (min-width: 601px)`. Touch and phone-width layouts keep density 0 and its touch targets. Form fields stop at -1, because -2 hides the label of the browser's filled "Filter" field.
- **Overlays:** menus and select panels use `surface-container-high`, a step above the panels, with a shadow; dialogs get a `level3` shadow. Docked panels keep their translucency.
- **Focus:** `mat.strong-focus-indicators`, a 2px ring in the accent colour.
- **lil-gui:** hover and focus are state layers over the widget colour, and the title uses `on-surface`.
- The `.mat-mdc-dialog-container` shape rule is replaced by `dialog-overrides`. No `.mat-mdc-*` or `::ng-deep` selectors are added.

## Outside `styles.scss`
- `inspector-shell.ts`: one line removes the docked or minimized inspector's shadow, so docked panels keep only a border. No token reaches that one surface.
- `app.scss` needed no change.

## Checks
- **Touch (375×812):** every button is the same size as on `develop` or larger. Inspector buttons stay 40px, toolbar buttons 32px.
- **Inspector state:** a lil-gui value changed, then tabs switched away and back; the value and the same lil-gui instance survive.
- **Focus:** the ring is visible on toolbar buttons, menu items, tabs and the search input in both themes.
- **Desktop (packed):** the titlebar maximize button toggles the window. The drag region CSS is unchanged; the drag gesture itself can't be automated.
- web:test (649), lint, format:check, build (initial 1.87 MB), `pnpm smoke`, `pnpm pack:desktop` and the full `pnpm run ci` pass on this branch.

## Review screenshots
Before and after, dark and light, over Aurora Veil (dark) and Poured Paint (bright): theme menu, export dialog, inspector and browser. They were shared in the review session and aren't attached here.

## Recommendation: magenta tertiary
Keep it. Next to neutral chrome it shows only on lil-gui string values and the "unsaved" status, where a second accent helps.

## Known limits
- The export dialog's outlined field labels are clipped at the top. This happens on `develop` too and isn't caused by this change.
- A "Sign in to use your shader library" snackbar sometimes flashes on first load; also on `develop`.

Plan: `docs/feature-plans/studio-visual-refresh-m1/` on `plans/studio-visual-refresh`.

body:
Task 01 of the studio visual refresh, milestone 1. The UI and icon fonts now ship with the app instead of coming from Google Fonts, so they render offline, in the desktop app, and on a cold cache.

## Changes
- Inter (variable, upright) and Material Symbols Outlined come from npm (`@fontsource-variable/inter`, `material-symbols`) and are added to the `styles` of both the web and desktop builds. The font files are separate assets, not inlined.
- `index.html` no longer links Roboto or Material Icons. The Google Fonts CSP entries stay for the editor's font picker.
- `mat.theme` typography and lil-gui's `--font-family` use Inter. Material's letter-spacing, tuned for Roboto, is zeroed so small labels don't look loose.
- Material Symbols is `MatIcon`'s default font set in the web and desktop configs; SSR merges the web config. Icon optical settings are set once, globally (`opsz` 20, `wght` 400).
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists Inter (OFL-1.1) and Material Symbols (Apache-2.0).

## Icon audit
Every string literal under `apps/web/src/app` was rendered with the real Symbols font in Chromium. All 94 icon names in use ligate, so no call sites changed. Five aren't in the package's canonical name list but still ligate as legacy aliases: `auto_awesome`, `expand_less`, `expand_more`, `launch`, `system_update`.

## Checks
- `pnpm smoke` has a new offline font check: in a fresh context with every non-local request aborted, Inter and Material Symbols load, no local font request fails, and no visible icon renders as text. Negative control: with the icon default removed, the check fails and lists the icons shown as text.
- Desktop: the packed app, launched with a fresh `userData` and the network routed to a dead proxy, loads both fonts from `shader-studio://bundle`, and the titlebar, toolbar and a dialog render their icons.
- web:test (649), lint, format:check, build, smoke and the full `pnpm run ci` pass.

## Sizes
- Web build output: 7.98 MB → 12.19 MB. The initial bundle is unchanged at 1.86 MB.
- Material Symbols Outlined: 4.0 MB. Inter latin: 48 KB (other subsets load only by `unicode-range`).

## Known limits
- The Symbols font is 4 MB and uses `font-display: block`, so icons stay blank until it loads on a slow first web visit. Subsetting to the icons in use would shrink it a lot, but every new icon name would then need the subset rebuilt.

Plan: `docs/feature-plans/studio-visual-refresh-m1/` on `plans/studio-visual-refresh`. Merge before M1-02.

body:
Task 03 of desktop sync milestone 2. Deleting a shader linked to the signed-in account now asks **Delete from this computer** or **Delete everywhere**; "everywhere" is queued so it works offline, and never destroys an account copy that changed since the last sync. Uses the conditional delete from #24 and the pull engine from #25.

## Behaviour
- `sync.remove(localId, mode)` (IPC), refused unless the shader is linked to the signed-in account (the renderer then falls back to the plain delete). Runs in the same queue as sync runs.
  - `local`: remote id added to `sync_ignored:<account>`, link dropped, local shader deleted. The account copy stays and is never pulled back.
  - `everywhere`: `{ remoteId, remoteRevision, name }` appended to `sync_tombstones:<account>`, link dropped, local shader deleted, then a run starts.
  - Account state is written before the local delete, so a crash in between leaves at worst an unlinked local copy.
- Each run sends tombstones first, identity-bound: `DELETE /api/shaders/:id?expectedRevision=N`.
  - 204/404 → tombstone dropped. 401/offline → kept, run stops as today. Other errors → kept and retried; the shader is neither pulled nor unlinked meanwhile.
  - 409 (changed on the web since the last sync) → tombstone dropped, the shader is pulled back as a linked local shader, and a `restored-after-delete` notice is shown once (snackbar, en/fr).
- Renderer: a three-button dialog (Cancel / Delete from this computer / Delete everywhere) for linked shaders; everything else keeps the existing confirm dialog. `ShaderStore.remove(id, removeRecord?)` lets the store run its usual cleanup after `sync.remove` deleted the shader.

## Tests
- `sync-service.spec.ts`: local-only delete ignores the id and sends no DELETE; everywhere deletes on the next run; offline everywhere deletes on reconnect; 404 drops, 500 keeps and blocks pull/unlink for that id; 409 pulls back with one notice; tombstones kept per account across a switch; a DELETE sent under A keeps its result under A then stops; refused for another account's link; a delete during a run pulling that shader waits and the link is not resurrected.
- Renderer spec: both choices route to `sync.remove` with the right mode, Cancel deletes nothing, refusal falls back to a plain delete, unlinked shaders keep the plain dialog.
- desktop:test (88), web:test (646), `pnpm check`, lint, typecheck, build:desktop, oxfmt on changed files pass. Locally nx needs `NX_NO_CLOUD=true` since the Nx Cloud setup on develop.

## Known limits
- `sync.remove` waits for a run in progress, so a delete during a long pull can take a moment.
- A 409 notice is recorded before the pull; if the web deletes the shader in between, the notice appears but nothing comes back.
- The delete condition is the revision only: an account copy whose only change is its thumbnail (thumbnails don't bump the revision) is still deleted.
- A shader in `error` gets the two-choice dialog even if it turns out unlinked (then the plain delete runs).

Plan: `docs/feature-plans/desktop-sync-m2/` on `codex/plan-desktop-sync`.

body:
Task 02 of desktop sync milestone 2. Manual testing of milestone 1 showed the desktop never read the account on its own: shaders deleted on the web stayed "synced", shaders created on the web never appeared, and a locally deleted linked shader left an orphan link. Every run now reads the account first.

## Run order
1. `GET /api/shaders` (templates excluded) — one request per run.
2. Push dirty links (unchanged from milestone 1).
3. Pull:
   - linked, remote revision higher, local clean → export, `replaceFromPayload`, then the account thumbnail (`setThumbnail` / `clearThumbnail`); link updated;
   - both sides changed → existing keep-both;
   - only the remote thumbnail changed → thumbnail pulled alone (link gains `remoteThumbnail`; older links pull it once);
   - remote not linked and not ignored → `importPayloads` (rename) and linked to the new local id;
   - linked remote id missing from the list → unlinked, local copy kept (`local-only`).
- A link whose local shader is gone (deleted locally) is dropped and its remote id goes to `sync_ignored:<account>`, so it is never pulled back; the account copy is untouched.
- Pulls are identity-bound like pushes and share the `{ done, total }` progress. A pull that replaces a local shader reports it in `replaced`, so an open editor reloads through the existing `ShaderStore.reloadReplaced` without losing its draft.
- "Synced" now means the last run found the shader in the account list; linked shaders show `pending` until then (startup, offline).

## Triggers
- Every 60 s while signed in (stopped on sign-out and dispose), and on window focus at most once every 15 s — both through `run()`, so they merge with a queued run. One line of wiring in `main.ts`.

## Tests
- `sync-service.spec.ts`: web-created shader pulled and linked (incl. local id collision, no re-export next run); web edit pulled with thumbnail and thumbnail removal; thumbnail-only change keeps the local revision; keep-both under the new order; web deletion → `local-only`; ignored id never pulled; locally deleted linked shader → ignored; account switch mid-pull keeps only the first export's result under the original account; timer + focus + manual run merge into one; focus throttle; timer stops on sign-out/dispose.
- desktop:test (73), web:test (641), `pnpm check`, lint, typecheck, build:desktop, oxfmt on changed files pass.

## Known limits (no data loss in any)
- A crash between a new pull's local import and saving its link imports it again next run (duplicate).
- A failed thumbnail write after a content pull makes the next run push the same content back and create a spurious `(conflict)` copy.
- The pulled revision comes from the list and may be older than the export; the next run re-pulls or a later push makes a spurious conflict copy.
- No renderer spec for the draft-keeping reload (existing code path, covered by its own spec).

Deletion choices ("Delete from this computer" / "Delete everywhere") come in task 03, which uses #24.

Plan: `docs/feature-plans/desktop-sync-m2/` on `codex/plan-desktop-sync`.

Task 01 of desktop sync milestone 2 (pull and deletion). Lets a sync client's queued "Delete everywhere" refuse to destroy an account copy that changed since it last read it.

## Changes
- `deleteShader(scope, id, expectedRevision?)` on both engines: check and delete in one statement (`AND revision = ?`) inside the library transaction. Nothing deleted + revision given → an owned row means `conflict`, no row means `not_found`.
- `ShaderLibrary.remove(id, expectedRevision?)`, validated with the existing `parseExpectedRevision`. Templates stay refused (`not_found`: the delete only matches owned rows).
- `DELETE /api/shaders/:id?expectedRevision=N`: anything but one positive-integer string → 400; stale → 409; documented (`@ApiQuery`, `@ApiErrors(400, 404, 409)`). Audit line only after a successful delete. Without the parameter, behaviour is unchanged.
- One-line change to the shared `ShaderRepository` interface for the new parameter.

## Tests
- Conformance (both engines): stale → conflict and the shader stays; matching → deleted; second delete → not_found; invalid revision → invalid; no parameter → deleted as before; foreign shader and template → not_found.
- REST: 400 for `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, `abc`, empty and repeated; 409 with no deletion and no audit line; 204 with the audit line.
- backend:test (103), server:test (65), typecheck (all projects), lint, oxfmt on changed files pass.

body:
## Summary

Stage 2 of the plugin plan: the feasibility gate for a sandbox shared by web and desktop. **It passes without changing the app-wide CSP.**

- `apps/web/src/app/plugins/plugin-sandbox.ts`: the host. It mounts a hidden `sandbox="allow-scripts"` **srcdoc** iframe (opaque origin). The frame's own CSP (`default-src 'none'; script-src <bootstrap>; worker-src blob:`) applies on top of the inherited app policy. The host exposes `start`, `call` (with a per-call timeout) and `terminate`.
- `apps/web/src/plugin-sandbox.js`: a static bootstrap. It builds the plugin's Worker from a `blob:` URL, transfers the host's `MessagePort` to it, and on the host's `stop` message calls **`worker.terminate()`** and confirms. Plugin code never runs in the frame.
- `terminate()` refuses calls and rejects pending ones immediately. It removes the frame once the stop is confirmed, or after a 1s fallback when no bootstrap is running.
- `apps/web/src/app/plugins/sandbox-probe.ts`: a hostile plugin, exposed as `pluginSandboxProbe()` in **dev builds only**.
- `tools/workspace/src/plugin-sandbox-smoke.ts`: drives the probe from `pnpm smoke`, which runs in CI.

A `srcdoc` rather than a served page because the server sends `frame-ancestors 'none'` / `X-Frame-Options: DENY` on everything it serves, so a served sandbox page could not be framed. A `srcdoc` is never fetched, so those headers don't apply.

## What the smoke asserts (Chromium, CI)

- Every in-page check passes: the plugin runs with origin `null`, the frame's document is `null` to the host, IndexedDB, CacheStorage and the Electron bridge are unavailable, a Worker loaded from the app's origin is refused, a forged second `start` is ignored, and the pending call and a later call are both rejected.
- **Per request:** fetching the app origin, a `no-cors` credentialed POST to `/api/shaders`, fetching the internet, a WebSocket to `localhost` and remote `importScripts` each raised a CSP violation **for their own URL**. No attempted URL appears in the browser's request log.
- **Termination, observed by the browser, not the closed port:** Playwright sees the plugin Worker close.
  - Chromium also reaps a removed frame's Worker, so a second run keeps the frame attached. The Worker must still die there, which only `worker.terminate()` can cause.
  - **Negative control:** the same run without `worker.terminate()` must show a surviving Worker, or the smoke fails.

### Mutations the check catches

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Bootstrap without `worker.terminate()` (the original bug) | fails: Worker survives with the frame attached |
| Host never sends `stop` | fails |
| Host neither stops nor removes the frame (the reviewer's reproduction) | fails three ways |
| Frame CSP loosened to `connect-src *` | fails, naming each leaked URL and its missing violation |

Something this showed: the app's inherited `connect-src 'self'` would allow requests to the app's own origin. It's the frame's own `default-src 'none'` that blocks them.

## Also checked by hand

The in-page checks, with no request leaving the browser, pass in **Firefox** (dev server) and in **Electron** through `shader-studio://bundle/`. Worker destruction is instrumented in Chromium only.

## Notes

- The Claude desktop browser pane blocks sandboxed subframe requests itself (`ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`), so run the probe in a normal browser.
- Firefox reports a blocked cross-origin Worker through an async `error` event instead of throwing.
- Not covered: WebKit/Safari, the production SSR server build, the Electron dev path (`localhost:4201`), and memory limits.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm smoke` passes, including the sandbox checks and the negative control
- [x] The four mutations above each fail the check
- [x] `tsc` for web and workspace-tools, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on changed files
- [x] Probe in Firefox, and in Electron through `shader-studio://bundle/`

Task 04 of the desktop account sync plan (milestone 1, wave 2), integrated on top of Task 03 (#20). Linked local shaders stay in sync with the account in the push direction; the local SQLite library remains the only thing the editor reads and writes.

## Behaviour
- **Upload on demand**: "Upload to account" on a shader row, "Upload all" in the desktop account menu (shown when signed in and a shader is local-only). First upload goes through `POST /api/import` (rename); the link stores `{ remoteId, remoteRevision, localRevision, localThumbnail }` in `storage_metadata` under `sync_links:<accountUserId>`. Templates never sync.
- **Automatic push of dirty linked shaders** (`revision > localRevision`): on sign-in, on `online`, 2 s after each local write, and with 5 s → 5 min backoff while the server is unreachable. Content via `PUT /api/shaders/:id/bundle` with `expectedRevision`; a changed thumbnail via `PUT /api/shaders/:id/thumbnail` (the bundle replace ignores thumbnails, #18). Runs are serialized.
- **409 → keep both**: the local edits are first saved as an unlinked `<name> (conflict)` copy, then the linked shader takes the account version (`replaceFromPayload` + `setThumbnail`); status `conflict-resolved` until the next edit.
- **404** → unlinked, kept locally (`local-only`). **401** → run stops, links and data kept, `reauth-required`. Links of another account show `other-account` and are never pushed.
- **UI**: a status icon per shader (only while signed in / reauth-required), "Retry" for a shader in `error`, a determinate "n / total" progress bar that never overlaps the loading bar.

## Integration
- Merge of `codex/desktop-sync-04` (e2daf46, 66f2b41, a05a93a) — only textual conflict in `main.ts` `ipc.loadAll` (both `account` and `sync` kept). The C4 stub is replaced by Task 03's `DesktopAccountSession`; `sync-service.ts` imports its types. Generated IPC bridge regenerated, not hand-merged.
- 0b1f8e4: "Upload all" moved to the account menu, "Retry" for errored shaders, one progress bar at a time, icons gated on account state.

## Tests / gate
- `sync-service.spec.ts` (real SQLite `ShaderLibrary` locally and behind a fake server, fake `AccountSession`): upload + link, dirty → push, thumbnail-only push, offline stays pending, 409 keep-both with no loss, 404 unlink, 401 stop, other-account never pushed, concurrent triggers run once.
- `pnpm gen:ipc`, lint, `pnpm check`, typecheck (all projects), `pnpm test` (desktop 60, web 638, …), `build:all`, `build:desktop`, `git diff --check` pass.

## Not verified — please run before merging
Manual E2E-1…5 from the plan were **not** run (need a real account and the protocol registered in Windows): upload two shaders, offline edit pushed on reconnect with progress, web+desktop concurrent edit → keep both, revoked session → reauth-required, second account receives nothing. `pnpm dev:server`, then `SHADER_STUDIO_ACCOUNT_URL=http://localhost:<port> pnpm dev:desktop`.
No renderer spec covers the new menu items / icon gating / progress rule (compile + typecheck only).

## Known limits
- An edit during a keep-both resolution (or a web edit between its two reads) can create an extra `(conflict)` copy — nothing lost.
- Local writes are detected by wrapping the library given to the shader IPC: a new `ShaderLibrary` write method must be added to `WRITES` in `sync-service.ts`.
- The links map is rewritten as one JSON value per change (`ponytail:` noted; a table is the upgrade path).
- A redirect from the server is treated like offline (backoff) rather than `error`.

Milestone 2 (pull, deletion unlink/delete-everywhere, offline delete queue) is deferred — see the plan.

Task 03 of the desktop account sync plan (milestone 1, wave 2). A desktop user signs in through the system browser and signs out; the main process holds an encrypted bearer session that the rest of the app reaches only through `AccountSession` (contract C4). Consumes the handoff merged in #19.

## Changes
- `apps/desktop/main/src/account/account-session.ts` (`DesktopAccountSession`): PKCE + `state`, opens `<accountUrl>/desktop/connect`, exchanges the code at `/api/desktop/token`, stores the token **only** through `safeStorage` (sign-in refused if unavailable). `fetch()` adds the bearer header, refuses URLs outside the account server and disables redirects; 401 → `reauth-required`. Sign-out calls the server (5 s timeout) and always deletes the stored token. Startup restores the session; offline keeps the cached user, a revoked session → `reauth-required`.
- Deep link `shader-studio://auth/callback` from `second-instance`, startup argv (primary instance) and macOS `open-url`; strict validation (43-char code, 16–128-char `state`, constant-time compare). The pending verifier/state is persisted encrypted so a callback that cold-starts the app still completes. `shader-studio://bundle/` serving unchanged.
- IPC `account.state/signIn/signOut/openAccountPage` + `account-changed` event; renderer `DesktopAccount` service and account menu (en/fr). `AuthService` and the routing coordinator are untouched.
- **Feature flag:** `SHADER_STUDIO_ACCOUNT_URL` injected at build time (https, or http on localhost). Unset → status `disabled`, protocol not registered, no menu: desktop behaviour unchanged.

## Tests
- `account-session.spec.ts` (11): wrong state rejected while the real sign-in keeps waiting, timeout, one attempt per callback, cold-start callback, token never on disk in plain text, 401 → reauth-required, revoked session at startup, offline startup keeps user, offline sign-out clears state.

`pnpm dev:server`, then `SHADER_STUDIO_ACCOUNT_URL=http://localhost:<port> pnpm dev:desktop`.

- Packaged builds register the scheme at runtime; `electron-builder.yml` has no `protocols:` entry (NSIS won't register/unregister it; macOS would need `CFBundleURLTypes`).

body:
Task 02 of the desktop account sync plan (milestone 1, wave 1). Lets a native client exchange a PKCE-bound one-time code for a normal, revocable bearer session, so the desktop never sees a password or a cookie.

## Flow
1. Desktop opens `/desktop/connect?state=…&code_challenge=…` in the system browser.
2. The page makes the user sign in if needed, then calls `POST /api/desktop/handoff { codeChallenge }` (browser cookie session, verified email) → `{ code }`, single-use, 60 s, stored hashed in `verifications`.
3. The page redirects to `shader-studio://auth/callback?code=…&state=…`.
4. Desktop calls `POST /api/desktop/token { code, codeVerifier }` → `{ token, user }` for a new session with user agent `Shader Studio Desktop`, then uses `Authorization: Bearer`.

## Security
- Code consumed before any check; every failure returns the same generic 400; S256 verification; token response `no-store`; codes and tokens never logged; one audit event `desktop.signed-in`.
- Token endpoint rate-limited (10/min per address).
- Only a **browser** session can request a handoff code, so a stolen desktop token cannot mint new sessions for itself.
- `bearer` plugin enabled **request side only**: its response side copies each new session token into a script-readable `set-auth-token` header, which would expose browser sessions to XSS. A spec asserts the header is absent.
- Origin/CSRF checks stay on globally. Better Auth only checks origin when the request carries a `Cookie`, so cookieless bearer requests (e.g. desktop sign-out) pass; a cookie request from an untrusted origin still gets 403 (both tested).

## Tests
- `desktop-handoff.spec.ts` (12 new): single use, 60 s expiry, wrong verifier (and code burned), anonymous/unverified refused, bad challenge, generic 400 on malformed input, rate limit, token authenticates `GET /api/shaders`, session listed as `Shader Studio Desktop`, 401 after revocation, bearer sign-out.

body:
Task 01 of the desktop account sync plan (milestone 1, wave 1). Gives sync clients what they need to detect changes and push a whole shader safely.

## Changes
- `ShaderSummary.revision` returned by both engines (SQLite, Postgres) and by the MCP summary schema.
- `ShaderLibrary.replaceFromPayload(id, payload, expectedRevision)`: one scoped transaction that replaces content, presets and textures, keeps `id` / owner / `kind` / `createdAt`, sets `revision = expectedRevision + 1`, and returns the record read inside the transaction.
- `PUT /api/shaders/:id/bundle` with `{ bundle, expectedRevision }` → `{ shader }`. Stale revision → 409, foreign/unknown → 404, template or collection bundle → 400.
- **The thumbnail is out of scope of the replace**: the bundle's thumbnail is ignored and the stored one is never touched. Previews go through `PUT /shaders/:id/thumbnail` (last-writer-wins, unchanged), so a replace can never lose a concurrent upload.

## Tests
- Conformance: revision exactly +1, presets/textures replaced, stale → conflict with no change, foreign → not_found, template refused, summary revision matches record, stored thumbnail untouched (null and non-null payload), a thumbnail uploaded after the client read N survives a replace at N.
- Conformance pins that update, preset save/delete, texture set/clear bump `revision` (thumbnail writes do not, on purpose: the web editor uploads the preview after a save without adopting a revision).
- REST (`router.spec.ts`): 200 with revision 2, 409, 404 as another user, 400 for a collection bundle, 401 without a session.
- Postgres suite only runs with `SHADER_TEST_DATABASE_URL`.

## Notes
- The MCP summary schema now requires `revision`: a newer MCP tool talking to an older app would fail to read the list.
- Request body limit is the same as `/import`.

Plan: `docs/feature-plans/desktop-sync-m1/` on `codex/plan-desktop-sync`.

body:
## Résumé

- ajoute l’authentification email/mot de passe avec Better Auth, vérification d’adresse et récupération de compte
- isole les shaders par propriétaire dans SQLite et PostgreSQL, avec migrations et commande de reprise des données existantes
- ajoute l’interface de connexion/compte, la gestion des sessions et les protections serveur associées
- conserve le mode desktop hors ligne avec un propriétaire local unique

## Retours de revue

- **Durée des sessions** : `expiresIn` = fenêtre d’inactivité (glissée toutes les heures via `updateAge`), plafond absolu imposé par un hook `databaseHooks.session.update.before` qui borne `expiresAt` à `createdAt + AUTH_SESSION_MAX_SECONDS`.
- **Docker Compose** : `AUTH_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL`, `AUTH_SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS`, `AUTH_SESSION_MAX_SECONDS`, `AUTH_CHECK_COMPROMISED_PASSWORDS` et `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT` sont transmis au service (vide = valeur par défaut).
- **Déconnexion** : `AuthService.signOut()` renvoie un `AuthResult` et ne vide l’état local qu’après invalidation côté serveur ; « Se déconnecter partout » garde le dialogue ouvert et affiche l’erreur si la révocation échoue.
- **Seconde revue** :
  - `updateAge` = moitié de la fenêtre d’inactivité (max 1 h), donc une session active glisse aussi avec une fenêtre ≤ 1 h. Tests d’intégration avec une config sous l’heure.
  - Révocation de sessions (`/revoke-session(s)`, `/revoke-other-sessions`) refusée avec `SESSION_NOT_FRESH` si la connexion date de plus de 15 min.
  - Le dialogue compte ne présente plus une erreur comme « aucune session » : si la connexion n’est plus fraîche, il redemande le mot de passe puis reprend l’action (liste ou déconnexion globale).
- **Troisième revue** : une connexion par-dessus une session existante (ré-authentification comprise) supprime la session que désignait le cookie entrant, donc plus d’appareil fantôme en double.
- **UI smoke** : le scénario s’inscrit sur une base jetable avant de piloter l’éditeur. Il a révélé trois bugs, corrigés ici :
  - le rendu SSR (sans cookie) publiait un snapshot vide après son `401`, donc un utilisateur connecté voyait une bibliothèque vide après rechargement ;
  - `INSPECTOR_TABS` n’incluait pas l’onglet post-processing (régression de `bb6e7c4`) ;
  - `nodemailer` et `drizzle-orm` n’étaient pas résolubles par le serveur SSR de dev (`ng serve`).

## Validation

- `pnpm lint` ✅
- `pnpm check` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm test` ✅
- `pnpm smoke` ✅ (local)
- `oxfmt --check` sur les fichiers modifiés par la PR ✅ (le `format:check` global signale encore des fichiers non touchés par cette PR)
- `pnpm build:all` : non relancé localement (couvert par le job CI `lint · check · typecheck · test · build`)

## Summary

Task 02 of the post-processing chain milestone (see `docs/feature-plans/post-processing-chain/README.md` and `02-effects-rack.md`), built on task 01's chain foundation (#7, merged). Ships the first user-facing configurable chain.

- `VignetteEffect` union member (intensity/softness/roundness, all clamped [0,1]) plus generic chain-mutation helpers (`addPostProcessingEffect`, `removePostProcessingEffect`, `setPostProcessingEffectEnabled`, `resetPostProcessingEffect`, `movePostProcessingEffect`, `withPostProcessingEnabled`)
- Resolution-independent, alpha-preserving Vignette `ShaderPass`; engine generalized to an ordered map of built passes keyed by effect type, with structural-rebuild vs. uniform-only-update distinction preserved for any mix of effects
- New Effects Rack (`post-processing-panel.ts`) in the Controls inspector: master bypass, add/remove (one per type), per-effect enable, reset, drag reorder plus accessible move-up/move-down; Bloom's old lil-gui folder removed
- Full-render preset icon/copy generalized (values-only presets untouched); Wallpaper export warning generalized to one message for any enabled post-processing effect
- `pnpm smoke` extended to add Vignette, reorder it, and exercise bypass through stable test IDs
- Fixed a real stale-closure bug found during manual testing: rapid consecutive setting edits on the same effect could clobber each other; fixed by re-reading the effect from the mutation's `render` argument instead of a captured template variable (regression test added)
- Fixed a latent leak where built passes weren't `dispose()`d, only the composer

Covers AC-RACK, AC-VIGNETTE, AC-PRESET, AC-COMPAT.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @shader-studio/shared test` - 448 passed
- [x] `pnpm --filter @shader-studio/web test` - 614 passed
- [x] `pnpm --filter @shader-studio/web typecheck` - clean

- [x] Manual E2E: legacy Bloom migration + legacy preset restore; Vignette add/reorder/persist across save-reload; master + per-effect bypass with no reload; values-only vs full-render preset semantics; generic Wallpaper export warning
- [x] Diff reviewed for scope (21 files, all within owned boundary)

## Known limitation

Drag reorder uses an adjacent-swap helper that only works because Phase 1 caps the chain at 2 effect types (Bloom, Vignette) - documented in code as an accepted simplification; will need real index-based reordering if a third effect type ships later.

## Summary

- add dormant WebGL GPU/CPU timing telemetry with total-frame and sampled per-pass costs
- report owned render-target and decoded-texture memory estimates plus latest compilation results
- add a persisted, translated Profiler inspector tab with conservative adaptive-resolution suggestions
- harden query, context, capture, active-renderer, resize, and live-workload lifecycle behavior
- keep the narrow Profiler table contained within the inspector instead of expanding the tab body horizontally

## Why

Shader authors need an honest view of frame cost and owned GPU allocations without blocking rendering or presenting CPU timing as GPU timing. The narrow inspector also exposed an intrinsic table-width overflow: five pass columns forced the preserved tab body wider than its rail.

## Implementation notes

GPU timing uses asynchronous `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2` queries and reports explicit warming, unsupported, and disjoint states. Profiling remains disabled until the Profiler tab is active. Memory values are labeled estimates and do not claim inaccessible driver VRAM.

The overflow fix constrains the panel’s flex/table sizing, uses a fixed table layout, and wraps long headers and pass names. At the reproduced 298 px inspector width, the Profiler host, tab body, and table now have matching `clientWidth` and `scrollWidth` values with no horizontal scrollbar.

## Validation

- full web suite: 54 files, 580/580 tests
- shared suite: 22 files, 416/416 tests
- focused Profiler panel: 20/20 tests
- web typecheck: pass
- i18n: 417 keys × 2 locales
- production web build: pass
- changed-path formatting and `git diff --check`: pass
- headless Profiler smoke: pass, observing `GPU timing is unavailable`
- live 298 px inspector measurement: no horizontal overflow

## Review

The complete feature range was independently reviewed and approved for a default-branch PR. Two non-blocking timer-adapter hardening ideas remain for later follow-up: exception-safe cleanup of an active query and bounded pending-query backpressure.

## Summary

- extract per-context texture ownership into `TextureManager`
- extract lazy bloom/composer lifecycle into `PostProcessing`
- prevent stale async composer loads and settings continuations from overriding the current state
- extract accepted-program compilation and probing into `PassCompiler`
- centralize accepted-pass uniform writes in `UniformRegistry`
- add non-owning channel binding through `ChannelBinder`
- keep `ShaderEngine` as the existing public facade

## Why

`ShaderEngine` previously owned texture caching, post-processing resources, compilation, accepted pass materials, and uniform broadcasting. These changes give each mutable resource a single owner while preserving the existing engine API and last-good-program behavior.

The post-processing fixes address two async races: a loader completing after disable/context invalidation, and an older settings continuation completing after a newer composer has been installed.

## Impact

Rendering consumers keep the same public API. Post-processing modules remain dynamically imported, texture and buffer ownership remain separated, failed shader candidates retain the last working material, and context restoration/disposal remain per-context and idempotent.

## Validation

Task 01 on the refreshed base:

- post-processing spec: 19 tests passed
- texture-manager spec: 14 tests passed
- multi-context spec: 9 tests passed
- multipass spec: 28 tests passed
- web typecheck passed with cache disabled

## What changed

- moved workspace document signals and computed projections into `DocumentState`
- moved project, config, parameter, and atomic MCP edits into `ProjectMutations`
- moved draft recovery and legacy project migration into `RecoveryFacade`
- moved initialization, SSR hydration, selection races, and record adoption into `SelectionLifecycle`
- kept `ShaderStore` as the compatible application-facing facade
- added focused state, mutation, recovery, migration, hydration, and selection-race tests

## Why

`ShaderStore` coordinated document state, editing, selection, persistence, and recovery in one large class. This PR lands the reviewed, dependency-complete store half of the god-class refactor so each state transition has a clear owner while existing consumers keep the same API.

The separate engine track is intentionally excluded from this PR because review found a pending dynamic-import/context-loss race in its post-processing owner. That work remains local for a fix round.

## Impact

Application consumers continue injecting and calling `ShaderStore`. Internally, the facade delegates to dedicated owners. Stale asynchronous selection responses can no longer overwrite the user's latest selection.
